Next thing you know he forwards my username to the admins as a spammer and BOOM! shadowban. It's ridiculous to give vengeful, highly opinionated mods that much power over the other users.

Most problems with online communities arise for either power issues (who decide what and how) or money ones. I think the use of sortition can help alleviate the power issue.

The basic idea is when a post or comment is reported for breaking a rule, a few active members are randomly selected and have to judge whether the content breaks the rule or not. The moderation is then automatically done according to the decision of the majority. There's a lot of ways to organize this in the details (how many people you should get in the jury, what kind of selection/report procedure, potential rewards/blames, etc.) but that's not really the point of this post.

So why sortition ?

  • It scales. More members, more posts, more moderators.
  • It implements political equality (isokratia). Each member has potentially its word to say about the moderation.
  • It's robust to corruption, and prevents censorship, manipulations, nepotism, etc.
